title: Tunisian crochet square
subtitle: A square motif worked in Tunisian simple stitch on a long hook, producing a dense woven fabric
excerpt: Tunisian crochet uses a long hook to pick up all stitches across the row in the forward pass, then works them off one by one in the return pass. The result is a dense, flat fabric with a distinctive woven grid on the surface. A 20-stitch by 20-row square in DK cotton gives a firm 10 cm tile.
sourceNotes: Tunisian (Afghan) crochet is documented in Weldon's Practical Needlework, Volume 1 (1885), Afghan stitch chapter (Internet Archive). Therese de Dillmont, Encyclopedia of Needlework (1886), Afghan crochet section.
heroPrompt: A Tunisian simple stitch crochet square in warm oatmeal DK cotton on a pale linen background, photographed flat from above in soft daylight. Dense woven-grid surface texture, slight curl corrected by blocking, 10 cm square.

crochet.gaugeText: Finished Tunisian square measures 10 × 10 cm in DK-weight cotton with a 5 mm Tunisian hook.

stitches.label: Tss in each ch — 20 loops on hook
yo + draw through 2 loops, repeat to end

glossaryTerms.definition: Insert hook from right to left through the vertical bar of the stitch below, yarn over and pull up a loop. Leave all loops on the hook (forward pass). On the return pass: yarn over, pull through 2 loops at a time to end.

content.text: to build a dense, flat fabric with a woven-grid surface. The forward pass picks up all 20 loops across the row; the return pass works them off two at a time. Unlike standard crochet, the work is never turned.

Tunisian fabric naturally curls at the edges before blocking. A 5 mm hook on DK yarn (larger than you would normally use) compensates for the tight gauge Tunisian produces. Block firmly on a mat — the fabric becomes flat and stable once wet-blocked.

attrs.title: Materials for one motif
attrs.body: About 14 g of DK-weight cotton. A 5 mm Tunisian (Afghan) hook — 30 cm long. Blocking mat.

content.text: Insert hook into 2nd ch from hook, yo, draw up loop (leave on hook). Rep in each ch to end. (20 loops on hook.)
Ch 1. *Yo, draw through 2 loops.* Rep from * to end. (1 loop remains on hook — the start of the next forward pass.)
Forward pass: insert hook through the vertical bar of each Tss below, draw up a loop for each. Return pass as above. After row 20: work a dc bindoff row along the top edge. Fasten off.
For colour patterns in Tunisian, try alternating yarn colours on the forward pass rows. Or work the interlocking crochet square for a different two-colour technique that avoids carrying yarn.
